title: Folks Ain't Roadblocks
evidence_boundary: The town-play and resistance-band language is metaphor for examining one's reactions and boundaries. It is not a claim that a person created, controls, or spiritually assigned other people.
desired_movement: From treating people as enemies blocking peace to examining what encounters reveal while preserving boundaries and other people's autonomy.
grounding: The episode returns to June's porch, Earl, two squirrels, and one pecan.
invitation: When somebody disturbs your peace, what role are they revealing—and what role are you choosing next?

legacy_reference.title: Ugh!! People!!
legacy_reference.visuals: retired low-grade animation; rebuild as premium June Oxley animation

risk_mitigations: Explicitly preserve other people's independent lives.
State that a kind fence remains a fence.
Make the viewer examine their role, not excuse mistreatment.

scenes.text: Earl came into the diner mad at humanity before the biscuits cooled.
scenes.query: premium animated small-town diner at dawn, same June Oxley character chuckling across from irritated Earl as biscuits steam

scenes.text: He said, “June, people are blocking my peace.” Like peace was a tractor and everybody parked in the field.
scenes.query: an old tractor blocked by a comically crowded field of parked farm equipment, no readable text

scenes.text: I told him, “Earl, you ain’t found enlightenment. You’ve just become allergic to witnesses.”
scenes.query: June Oxley leaning in with a crooked grin while Earl reacts at the diner counter

scenes.text: He did not enjoy that. Nearly buttered his napkin in protest.
scenes.query: Earl dramatically buttering a folded napkin while June watches, warm animated diner motion

scenes.text: See, people can feel like a town play where nobody learned their lines and everybody brought a tambourine.
scenes.query: a tiny rural town transforming into a theatrical stage while locals enter carrying one unnecessary tambourine

scenes.text: The loud neighbor enters early. Your ex returns for an unnecessary second act.
scenes.query: a loud neighbor bursts through one stage door while an ex returns through another marked only by color

scenes.text: Somebody cuts you off in traffic, then performs the ancient ritual of pretending mirrors do not exist.
scenes.query: animated pickup traffic scene where a driver cuts in, then carefully avoids every mirror

scenes.text: And there you are, declaring the whole cast defective.
scenes.query: June in an empty director chair looking at a chaotic cast while a red reject stamp breaks apart, no readable text

scenes.text: But here is the country-sized twist: folks are not merely obstacles in your scene.
scenes.query: townspeople move from roadblocks into distinct travelers on intersecting paths

scenes.text: They show where patience leaks, pride swells, and kindness still needs suspenders.
scenes.query: animated patience leaking from a bucket, pride inflating a vest, and kindness held up by suspenders

scenes.text: That is metaphor, not proof that you invented other people.
scenes.query: several town houses light up independently, each containing a different private story

scenes.text: Everybody has their own life, their own hurt, and probably batteries that fit nothing.
scenes.query: a junk drawer full of mismatched batteries rolling around as different townspeople search for the right one

scenes.text: But every meeting still gives useful evidence about the role you are playing when the curtain rises.
scenes.query: a spotlight follows June's own boots and posture instead of the other actors

scenes.text: Some folks reveal tenderness. Some reveal the part rehearsing arguments in the shower.
scenes.query: steam-filled shower with a silhouette rehearsing an argument to shampoo bottles

scenes.text: Some arrive like resistance bands for the soul—annoying, stretchy, and included with membership.
scenes.query: colorful resistance bands stretching between porch posts while June tries not to get snapped

scenes.text: Earl asked whether that meant loving everybody unconditionally.
scenes.query: Earl raises one suspicious eyebrow at June over coffee, same animated diner world

scenes.text: I said, “No, sir. A fence can be kind and still remember why it was built.”
scenes.query: a well-built wooden fence opens a friendly gate but keeps the property boundary clear

scenes.text: Doing right by people does not require handing them your porch keys.
scenes.query: June closes his palm around porch keys while politely waving from behind the gate

scenes.text: It means refusing cruelty as your costume because somebody else dressed poorly.
scenes.query: a harsh costume hanging unused while June chooses simple work clothes from a porch hook

scenes.text: Sometimes the lesson is patience. Sometimes distance. Sometimes admitting you enjoy being right too much.
scenes.query: a rural crossroads with symbols for patience, distance and humility, no readable text

scenes.text: The town play gets clearer when you stop trying to fire the entire cast.
scenes.query: June puts away a comic firing stamp while the town cast resumes the play

scenes.text: You start asking what each scene shows about your own performance.
scenes.query: a stage mirror reflects June's posture, tone and choices rather than other people's faces

scenes.text: Back on the porch, Earl watched two squirrels fight over one pecan and said humanity looked familiar.
scenes.query: two squirrels tug one pecan on a porch rail while Earl and June watch in warm evening light

scenes.text: So when somebody disturbs your peace, what role are they revealing—and what role are you choosing next?
scenes.query: same June Oxley in rocking chair at dusk, leaning toward the viewer as the town settles behind him
